t: Section 1345 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4081) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(d) FEMA Authority on Transfer of Policies.—Notwithstanding any other provision of this title, the Administrator may, at the discretion of the Administrator, refuse to accept the transfer of the administration of policies for coverage under the flood insurance program under this title that are written and administered by any insurance company or other insurer, or any insurance agent or broker.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that because insurance companies, agents and brokers are mentioned, outside parties are involved in a federal decision. But the provision only gives the FEMA Administrator unilateral discretion to refuse policy transfers. It requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, so the insurers are subjects of the decision rather than participants in it.
fable.s: the Administrator may, at the discretion of the Administrator, refuse to accept the transfer of the administration of policies for coverage under the flood insurance program

qwen_block.w: This section grants the FEMA Administrator discretionary authority to refuse a transfer of policy administration from private insurers. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from the private insurers or the public before making this decision. The interaction described is a unilateral administrative action by a federal official, not a participatory process involving outside parties in the decision-making.
qwen_block.s: the Administrator may, at the discretion of the Administrator, refuse to accept the transfer of the administration of policies for coverage under the flood insurance program under this title that are written and administered by any insurance company or other insurer, or any insurance agent or broker.

opus.w: The section lets the FEMA Administrator decide alone, "at the discretion of the Administrator," whether to refuse transfers of policy administration. It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. It might seem like participation because insurance companies, agents, and brokers are named, but they are only the parties the decision affects. Nothing gives them a role in making it.
opus.s: the Administrator may, at the discretion of the Administrator, refuse to accept the transfer of the administration of policies

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the FEMA Administrator discretionary authority to refuse the transfer of flood insurance policies. It does not require any consultation, public comment, hearing, or coordination with the insurance companies or other outside parties before making that decision. The decision is made solely at the discretion of the federal official.
qwen_chat.s: the Administrator may, at the discretion of the Administrator, refuse to accept the transfer of the administration of policies
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Administrator's discretion to refuse a transfer involves a decision-making process that could implicitly involve consultation with the insurer. However, the text itself does not mandate or even suggest any consultation, hearing, or comment period. It simply grants the Administrator the authority to refuse. There is no requirement for the outside party (the insurer) to participate in the decision.
